summary: CoordinatingSessionClient.reopen(target) posts to /coordinating-session/reopen with the x-coordinating-target header and reuses the existing openedIn boundary model for a 202, or productError for a refusal; useCoordinatingSession().reopen() reads the held target from heldRef and runs the call through the existing runOpening state machine, answering the shared BLOCKED_OPENING refusal with no fetch when nothing is held. The brief's TDD line named all three new tests as living "in client.test.ts", but the third one (reopen with no held session sends nothing) is a hook-level guard the client function cannot express on its own, since the client always sends whatever target it is given; I put it in useCoordinatingSession.test.ts instead, which the brief's own Files line already listed as (modify), and left client.test.ts with the two tests that are genuinely about the wire call. summary: Home renders FocusedSession for every held session (live, ended or unresumable) and only the start form otherwise; FocusedMode.of no longer takes planHeld/activePlans/epicGroom, and its own claims() helper is gone with the workflow-adoption machinery it served. FocusedSession now takes held: HeldRead instead of story/repo/target, draws CentredSession only when terminal is non-null, and passes GateBand a hardcoded dispatched=0 per the task's own contract, a real (temporary) loss of the dispatched-count display that Task 4+ owns. The start branch's StartPlanForm is always isLocked=false with no request/isMutationBlocked, since the restore/reconciliation state it served no longer exists. Fifteen classic-view-only test files are deleted; the six named files (startPlan, epicGroom, specFreeze, coordinatingSession, focusedSession, shell) are trimmed rather than rewritten. One correction to the brief: helpers.tsx's `editable` is kept (unexported, as it already was) because typeTicket/typePath still call it — deleting it as the brief said would break both, so I kept the behavior it named as fully removable and reused the plan's real intent instead. Three groups of surviving tests needed real fixes rather than trims: (1) two Home.epicGroom/specFreeze tests split in half to drop a second "Implementación"-heading scenario that has no equivalent until the milestone board lands, with the surviving half kept as its own test; (2) three tests across those same files and Home.coordinatingSession that asserted a disabled Ticket field now assert the field is absent, since a held session never shows the start form at all; (3) Home.coordinatingSession's five 'Cerrar sesión' cases now read 'Cancelar la sesión', the one button FocusedSessionHeader offers for every held state, and two of its tests (`refuses to open a second brainstorming while one is live`, the original `reads the coordinating session through a single poller`) were passing only because they asserted on the transient pre-connect paint rather than steady state — I rewrote both to wait for the focused heading first, and to assert on the steady state instead. `npx vitest run src/pages/home --maxWorkers=4` (9 files, 85 passed) and `npm run build` both pass; two hand mutations (forcing FocusedMode to require only 'live', and reverting the client's POST path) were caught by the new tests before being reverted. A full-suite run turns up exactly one unrelated failure, `__tests__/yardstick.test.ts`'s git-tracking check, which compares the walked filesystem against `git ls-files`; it fails only because the 15 deletions and the 1 new file aren't staged yet (all 859 per-file yardstick rules pass) and should clear once ct-step stages the reported paths.

summary: At step 4, FocusedSession swaps CentredSession for MilestoneBoard, which lists every issue of the milestone under the region "Issues del milestone" with "X de N entregadas"; a running line reads "<step label> · Tarea X de Y · mm:ss", dropping the task clause when task is null. One clarification I made past the letter of the Contract: it types useMilestoneProgress as returning `MilestoneProgressOutcome | null`, but the prose right after says "the hook also returns reread()" — those two sentences cannot both be literally true, so I made it return `{ read, reread }` to honor the second sentence, since a signature that dropped reread() entirely could not satisfy what Task 6/7 need from it. MilestoneBoardProps and SliceLineRowProps carry onTalk, story and onClose exactly as the Contract specifies, even though nothing in this task's own UI calls them yet (Task 6 wires onReread, Task 7 wires onTalk to something other than null, Task 9 wires onClose to something other than the plain lifecycle.close forward I gave it) — the same kind of placeholder Task 3 already left with GateBand's dispatched=0. Needs-person lines get a bare "Necesita atención" placeholder pending Task 6's real markup. Three mutations (forcing MilestonePolling.intervalFor to always return the fast interval, and zeroing ElapsedTime's minutes component) were introduced by hand and both were caught by the new tests before being reverted. `npx vitest run src/pages/home --maxWorkers=4` (9 files, 88 passed) and `npm run build` both pass with no regressions.

summary:
Task 6 implemented test-first. `SliceRecovery` (new) reads `ActivePlansClient.get()`, finds the `uncertain` plan matching `{repo, issue}`, and calls `cleanup` or `recover`; refuses with `slice-recovery-not-found` when no such plan exists. `SliceLineRow` replaces the bare `Necesita atención` placeholder with an `AttentionBlock` carrying the exhaustive copy per attention kind (veto/uncertain/partial/unreadable) and exactly one action: `Hablar con la sesión` (disabled when `onTalk` is null) for veto/partial/unreadable, or the recovery button (label from `SliceRecovery.LABELS`) for uncertain, which calls `SliceRecovery.run` and then `onReread`, showing a refusal detail on failure. `MilestoneBoard` shows a warning `Banner` above the list when any line has `baselineRed`. Extended `ImplementationBackend` in `Home.implementation.test.tsx` with `/active-plans`, `/recover-plan`, `/cleanup-plan` scripting and added the three required tests (`it.each` over the four attention kinds, the baseline-notice test with one red line and none, and the recovery-button test asserting the exact `/recover-plan` body with the plan's agent).

TDD: wrote all six new test cases first, confirmed RED for the right reason (`Unable to find an element with text/role`, no import errors), then implemented. `npx vitest run src/pages/home/__tests__/Home.implementation.test.tsx --maxWorkers=4` (13 passed) and `npx vitest run src/pages/home --maxWorkers=4` (9 files, 96 passed) both green; `npm run build` passes with no regressions.

Hand-mutation sweep (each introduced, confirmed red, then reverted and reconfirmed identical): (1) duplicated the `Hablar con la sesión` button — caught by the "exactly one action" length assertion; (2) changed `SliceRecovery.LABELS.observe` — caught by the uncertain case's button-name assertion; (3) forced `SliceRecovery.run` to always call `cleanup` instead of dispatching on `asked.action` — caught by the recovery test's exact `/recover-plan` body assertion (times out since `/cleanup-plan` isn't scripted); (4) hardcoded `baselineRed = false` in `MilestoneBoard` — caught by the baseline-notice test.

Declared gap (test nobody wrote, not a missing line): the per-kind hint/detail text (`VETO_HINT`, and the `uncertain`/`partial`/`unreadable` `.detail` pass-through) is rendered but not independently asserted beyond the title — the brief's TDD/Tests section only asked for the two `it.each`/notice tests plus the recovery-button test, and this is a direct backend-string pass-through with no branching logic of its own.

Judgment call: the brief's `**Files:**` line for Task 6 does not list `SliceLineRow.css`; I added a small stylesheet block (`.slice-line-row__attention*`) for the new markup, matching the file's existing per-block CSS convention (every other structural class in this component already has one). Flagging in case this is considered outside the declared file boundary.

task_name: Hablar con la sesión opens the terminal over the list
summary:
Task 7 implemented test-first. New `SessionPanel` (`role="dialog"`, `aria-label="Sesión coordinadora"`) holds `Volver a la lista` and `CentredSession`, laid over the board with `position: absolute; inset: 0` in its own CSS. `FocusedSessionHeader` gained an optional `onTalk?: (() => void) | null` prop: the `Hablar con la sesión` button renders before `Cancelar la sesión` only when `onTalk !== undefined` (omitted outside step 4), disabled when `onTalk === null`. `FocusedSession` keeps `talking` state (`useState`), computes `talkAction = terminal !== null ? () => setTalking(true) : null`, passes it as `onTalk` to the header only at the `implementation` step (`undefined` otherwise) and to `MilestoneBoard` (which already threads `onTalk` down to each `SliceLineRow` since Task 6). At step 4 the board and the (conditionally rendered) `SessionPanel` are siblings, so the list stays mounted while the panel overlays it.

TDD: added `it('Hablar con la sesión opens the terminal in a panel over the list')` and `it('Volver a la lista closes the panel')` first, confirmed RED for the right reason (`Unable to find role="button" and name "Hablar con la sesión"`), then implemented. `npx vitest run src/pages/home/__tests__/Home.implementation.test.tsx --maxWorkers=4` (15 passed) and the full `npx vitest run src/pages/home --maxWorkers=4` (9 files, 98 passed) are green; `npm run build` also passes.

Hand-mutation sweep (each introduced, confirmed red, then reverted and reconfirmed identical): (1) forced the `SessionPanel` render condition in `FocusedSession` to always be `false` — caught by the "opens the terminal" test failing to find the dialog; (2) stubbed the `Volver a la lista` button's `onClick` to a no-op — caught by the "closes the panel" test still finding the dialog; (3) forced the header's `onTalk !== undefined` condition to always be `false` — caught by the "opens the terminal" test failing to find the button at all.

Judgment call: the `**Files:**` line does not include `FocusedSession.css`, and `.focused-session` has no `position` declared, so `SessionPanel`'s `position: absolute` positions against whatever ancestor up the tree happens to be positioned, not necessarily the board's own box. No test exercises real layout (jsdom has no layout engine), so this doesn't affect the task's verification, but the visual overlay may need `position: relative` added to `.focused-session` in a later task that is allowed to touch that file.
